title: Walter Barnes and George Baquet
summary: Walter Barnes of Natchez was a good clarinetist who died in a fire; George Baquet was a sweet player and parade man, while Big Eye Louis was the real band man.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Walter Barnes was away? Where was he from? He was from St. Charles or Lake Charles. He got killed in a fire.
In Natchez. He was a clarinet player? Was he a good one? Good clarinet player.
Did he play around New Orleans much? All those fellas, they didn't see him. They come on down here. We went on up there.
Did the Walter Barnes live here or did he just come in on gigs? No, no. He stayed up there in Natchez.
How about Bacay? What were some of the things you liked about the way Bacay played? Peter Bacay? No, George Bacay. What? Bacay. Bacay. Oh, George? Yeah.

Well, I'll tell you how George was. He was a, to me he was a sweet clarinet player. You know, he just took his time and made that. You know, he didn't rough it out. But he had that one way. Now for a band man, he wasn't that much, he ain't a band man. But he was a tough man in the parade. And you could hear him way down there but so sweet. Now your man, your good band man, real band man, that was Louis, which we called Big Eye Louis. In the orchestra you mean? Yeah. In the orchestra. That's really, Charlie can tell you that. He's a real band man. You like this style, huh? What kind of a style did he have then? Yeah, the swing style, the sweet style. It's like I play, I don't play one way. I play different. I wish I could. I'll have to shorten up a little bit. I'll try to shorten up to get some of my stuff. Yeah. Different way of playing, you know. Not one style play. I never liked one style play.
